linkedin:
> It means the request conflicts with the current state of the resource.

The four common cases are creating something that already exists, updating a record somebody else changed first, violating a state rule such as cancelling an already-shipped order, and submitting the same operation twice. If you are receiving one, read the response body, because a well-built API explains which conflict occurred. If you are building one, catch unique constraint violations and return 409 with a clear message rather than letting them surface as a 500.

Read the full guide: https://www.kloudbean.com/blog/409-conflict-error/
